reviews.name: opus-a
reviews.visualDeltaReview:
Busy conversations match the baseline layout, and the project badges are now fully saturated with legible white initials. Checking the primary Save button on the Agent screens.# CI correction delta (council62): verdict unchanged

**Score stays 9/10, ship.** None of the changes cause a regression that needs fixing.

## What I checked
- **The diff:** all seven files in `/tmp/dovo-ci62-final.diff`, plus the matching current-checkout source (`button.tsx`, `conversation.tsx`, `project-icon.tsx` and the colour palette in `workspace.ts`).
- **Frames, 4 of the 20:** `busy-conversation-dark`, `busy-conversation-light`, `agents-dirty-dark` and `agents-dirty-compact-light`.
- **Agent traversals:** `interactions.json` has 8 `unobstructed` entries and none are `false`.
- I didn't open the other 16 supplement frames, and I ran nothing.

## The three production fixes
1. **Primary button border:** `border border-transparent` was added to the default variant. Every size uses a fixed height (`h-8`, `h-7`, `h-10`) and the touch size uses `min-h-11`, so the extra border doesn't change button height. It only takes 1px from the padding area on each side, which isn't visible.
   - In both Agent frames, "Save changes" keeps the baseline size and position, with no visible border line in either theme.
   - Disabled styling is still opacity-only, so the 2px shift can't come back from the default variant.
2. **ProjectIcon colours:** the badges now use the palette colour directly with white text. My own WCAG luminance check of all ten colours gives at least 4.5:1. The two closest are `#007dbc` (about 4.5:1) and `#008577` (about 4.5:1); the rest are about 4.6–5.7:1.
   - That bar is the right one here, because the initials are 9px bold, which counts as normal-size text under WCAG.
   - In both busy-conversation frames the ST, OP and CL badges are visibly more saturated and easier to read, and nothing else in the layout changed.
3. **Conversation keyboard scrolling:** the scroll viewport now gets `tabIndex = 0` inside the existing layout effect, before the ResizeObserver is set up. It's added to the existing tab order rather than placed ahead of it, and no focus ring shows at rest in either frame.
   - The scroll element is inside the `role="log"` region rather than being that element.
   - I didn't see the focus ring itself in any frame, so I'm relying on the browser's default `:focus-visible` outline there.

## Test-script changes (verification note, not a required change)
- **Terminology:** the "task" → "thread" renames in the tests match the product terms.
- **Layout stability test:** it now starts in the dirty state and asserts that clean desktop forms omit Save/Discard while showing a status cue. It also checks that returning to dirty puts Save back in the same position. That matches the explicit-save design I accepted in the original review.
- **Jira catalog check:** it now only asserts that an unconfigured Jira source has Filters disabled and shows Connect Jira. Configured-filter coverage is said to have moved to `check-jira-views-browser.mjs`, which I didn't inspect or see a log for. So the Jira filter chips are less directly verified in this evidence set than before. That doesn't affect the UI verdict.
reviews.keyboardFollowup:
# Keyboard scroll fix (same delta): verdict unchanged

**Still 9/10, ship.** The fix doesn't introduce a regression that needs changing.

## The handler (`conversation.tsx:50-64`)
- **Scope:** it reacts only when the scroll viewport itself has focus (`event.target === viewport`). Key presses in the composer, links, buttons or code-block controls inside the transcript are ignored, and Alt/Meta combinations are excluded.
- **Behaviour:** ArrowUp, PageUp and Home call the library's existing `stopScroll()`. The handler doesn't call `preventDefault` or `stopPropagation`, so the browser still does the scrolling itself.
- **Lifecycle:** it's registered in a separate `useLayoutEffect` keyed on `scrollRef`/`stopScroll`, with a matching `removeEventListener` in the cleanup. Re-renders can't stack duplicate listeners.
- **Downward keys:** End, PageDown and ArrowDown are untouched, so going back to the bottom re-engages auto-follow normally.
- The production change is still confined to the same three files.

## The test (`check-thread-scroll-browser.mjs`)
- It asserts that the viewport has `tabindex="0"`, focuses it, and confirms it is the focused element.
- It presses PageUp and waits until the view is more than 100px from the bottom, then presses End and waits for it to reach the bottom again.
- That covers the defect you described. I didn't run it; your report that the whole scroll suite passes is the only run evidence I have.

## Non-blocking notes
1. **Shift+Space isn't handled.** Browsers also scroll up on Shift+Space, and the handler doesn't cover it, so auto-follow could still pull the view back in that case. It's an uncommon key for scrolling a transcript, so I don't consider it a required change.
2. **The test could pass on a momentary scroll.** The 100px check is polled until it succeeds. If auto-follow snapped the view back a frame later, the test would still pass. Re-checking the distance after a short pause, before pressing End, would prove the view actually stays put.

reviews.keyboardFollowup:
**My delta verdict stands: 9/10, gate met, ship. This fix doesn't introduce any required regression.**

**The handler (`packages/web-ui/src/conversation.tsx:50-64`)**
- **Scope:** it only acts when `event.target === viewport`. Keys pressed in the composer, buttons or links inside the log never reach it.
- **Keys:** ArrowUp, PageUp and Home. Alt and Meta combinations are excluded, so OS and browser shortcuts aren't affected.
- **Action:** it calls the existing `stopScroll()` and nothing else. It doesn't call `preventDefault`, so the browser still does the actual scrolling.
- **Cleanup:** `removeEventListener` runs when the effect re-runs or the component unmounts.

**The test (`scripts/check-thread-scroll-browser.mjs:130-141`)**
- It asserts `tabindex="0"`, focuses the viewport and confirms it is `document.activeElement`.
- After PageUp it waits until the view is more than 100px above the bottom, so it checks real movement, not just that the key was pressed.
- After End it waits for the existing `bottom()` check.
- The neighbouring checks still run: composer-only growth stays at the bottom, and focus or reading old turns detaches following.

**Limits**
- I read the handler and that test section only. I didn't run the suite, so "entire scroll suite passes" is your report, not something I checked.
- I didn't re-open the updated eight-file diff. My reading of the handler and test comes from the current checkout files, and I took your word that production changes are still limited to the same three files.
- The `bottom()` check confirms the scroll position after End. I didn't trace whether following itself resumes afterwards.
- Shift+Space (page up) doesn't call `stopScroll()`. It isn't in the bug you described and it isn't required; I'm noting it only for completeness.
